fields.label: Description
fields.value: Recording of the April 1960 Convention of the AFL-CIO Mississippi Labor Council. In this recording, Chairman Ramsey leads the convention through a series of speeches by council members and guests on the labor movement’s involvement in political action, women’s involvement in the labor movement, labor disputes, and public relations.

00:00:03:1 - 00:00:19:1
Unknown
Will, the sergeant at arms, please ask the delegates to come in. lot to do and a short time to do it in a convention will be in order.

00:00:22:1 - 00:01:01:0
Unknown
I'll ask the delegates to please rise and receive the invocation from Rabbi Phillips. The Phillips is Almighty God and Father with deep humility and sincere gratitude. We are approaching the humility since we know that except the Lord build the whole of the river in vain, that build it with gratitude because we know that all our blessings commit thy hands.

00:01:02:0 - 00:01:43:1
Unknown
The men and women assemble here are a proud part of our great country's labor force. They work and toil that nobody should go hungry and naked. We want them not only as material gains, but as to recognition by all their fellow men for their contribution to human society. May all citizens of this great country of ours never be misled into believing that the ills of society are the law of nature, which cannot be changed by men.

00:01:43:1 - 00:02:25:0
Unknown
Make all our fellow men aware of their duty to make the needful sacrifices to right homes and sheer blessings. Major deliberations of the Mississippi Labor Council, which come to a close today, be a step forward and the goal of the AFL-CIO to secure for labor, equality, justice and a recognition that thy blessing rests upon this Assembly and Mississippi Labor Council on the very blessing go forward and help to build a better world.

00:02:26:0 - 00:03:09:0
Unknown
Amen Rabbi, we are certainly happy to have you with us this morning. And we would like to extend to you an invitation to spend the rest of the day with us and participate in our convention activities. However, if you see fit and are pressed for time, then feel free to leave any time that you have to.

00:03:11:1 - 00:03:36:1
Unknown
Before we begin this morning, I want to advise the delegates that this being the last day of your convention, you have much work yet to do and it depends upon how fast you accomplish that work. As to how soon you get away from here this afternoon or tonight.

00:03:41:0 - 00:05:09:1
Unknown
It was my understanding that Judge Ramsey would be here this morning to pinch hit for Senator Bordron Is has he showed up yet? Has Sister Murray showed up yet? Then in the absence of the scheduled speakers, we will call up the chairman of the Education Committee and proceed to dispose of some of our resolutions. And in the event that the speaker shows up, we will then suspend that operation and allow them to address the convention Brother Gray of the Public Relations and Education Committee.

00:05:11:0 - 00:05:31:0
Unknown
Good morning to everyone. We're happy to be here this morning. I'd say we had a lovely evening. We will turn to resolution number 14.

00:05:35:0 - 00:06:14:1
Unknown
This resolution submitted by James E. Clark Public Relations, Vice President. Subject is Community relations. Whereas, the labor movement, by its very nature, is dedicated in advancing the common welfare of our nation, the communities in which we serve, and where as we have a mutual interest existing through the natural community. Participation of our members in their religious and educational institutions, farm, veteran, fraternal and civic organization.

00:06:16:0 - 00:06:56:0
Unknown
Whereas, the convention of the AFL-CIO created a Community Services Committee to carry out a vigorous program through union and community channels designed to encourage labor participation in community affairs and to receive public recognition of Labor's efforts in community life. And. WHEREAS, as an active Community Services Committee. Program is conducted through the local central Labor councils. Labor has bettered its public relation program in addition to making recognized contributions to the community welfare.

00:06:57:0 - 00:07:32:0
Unknown
And the result has been recognition and acceptance of the AFL CIO program. Now therefore, be it resolved that the Mississippi Labor Council, AFL CIO Convention assembled in Vicksburg, Mississippi, April 25 through 27, 1960, does hereby strongly urge every Central Labor Council in the State of Mississippi to create an active Community Services Committee. And we have a correction here.

00:07:33:0 - 00:08:15:1
Unknown
Be it further resolved. Change the word finally to further that each local union actively cooperate with and participate in the community services program of city and state AFL-CIO councils with which they are affiliated. Mr. Chairman, the committee concurred in this resolution. I move that we accept this resolution. You've already committed to report the motions to adopt. We have a second to the motion.

00:08:17:0 - 00:09:03:0
Unknown
We're having a discussion on the motion of not all in favor of the motion. Let it be known by saying I am all opposed with the same sign motion carried and so ordered. Continue Brother Chairman Next will be resolution number 15 submitted by James E. Clark, Public Relations Vice President. Subject is publicity. Whereas, the many affairs of our local unions and central labor unions are of interest to the general public, as well as union members and.

00:09:03:0 - 00:09:39:0
Unknown
WHEREAS, the many contributions of organized labor and the community services field, collective bargaining area and others are not effectively reported. And. WHEREAS, the general public receives in most cases, only the news concerning organized labor, which is controversial or concerning strikes and disputes. And. WHEREAS, meetings and general activities of our local and central unions will receive better support when publicized in our newspapers, radio and television stations.

00:09:40:1 - 00:10:09:0
Unknown
Now, therefore, be it resolved that each local union and central body in the State of Mississippi is hereby urged to assign such duties to one person in each local and central Labor Council. And be it further resolved that such person prepare and release to the press and their area any such news of local meeting, central labor union meetings, community matters which are acted upon.

00:10:09:1 - 00:10:43:1
Unknown
Participation in charitable drives and other such activities as well as results of collective bargaining. And be it finally resolved that such news releases be prepared so as to contain factual information that may be signed by some responsible union official. Mr. Chairman, the committee has concurred in this resolution. We moved to adopt this resolution. You've heard the committee's report, the motion is to adopt the resolution.

00:10:44:0 - 00:11:01:1
Unknown
We add a second. I believe we're having a discussion on the motion. Not all in favor of the motion. Let it be known by saying I all opposed by the same signed motion carried and so ordered continue brother chairman.

00:11:05:0 - 00:11:45:1
Unknown
Resolution number 16 submitted by Tom Knight, Educational Vice President, Education. Whereas it is a known fact that a large number of the members of organized labor in Mississippi do not have a full understanding of all phases of trade union movement. And. WHEREAS, the record of our neighboring states reflect that a broad educational program of the Central Council of the Council has been most helpful to the members in those states to overcome this common problem.

00:11:46:1 - 00:12:38:1
Unknown
And. WHEREAS, it is essential that we take necessary steps through the Mississippi Labor Council, AFL CIO to educate our members in such a manner so that we can improve our overall operation as trade unions and to meet this objective. It will be necessary that a complete educational program designed for local use be drafted. Now therefore, be it resolved that the delegates assembled here direct the Executive Committee to draft an educational program on subjects that are of interest and are needed by the members of organized labor in Mississippi, and be it further resolved that this program be made available as soon as possible to the membership and not the schools be handled through the various central

00:12:38:1 - 00:13:11:0
Unknown
local labor unions where possible, and they shall be conducted under the supervision of the Vice president. The Mississippi Labor Council, AFL CIO in charge of education. Be it further resolved that each affiliated local, each affiliated central labor, union and local create on an active educational committee to assist the Mississippi Labor Council in planning and carrying out this educational program for the welfare of our members.

00:13:11:0 - 00:13:41:0
Unknown
And the labor movement may find resolved that the local unions affiliated be urged to participate in these schools, and that a complete report of educational activities of the Council be given at the next convention of the Mississippi Labor Council. Mr. Chairman, the committee concurred in this resolution. I move to adopt this resolution. You've heard the committee's report. The motion is to adopt the resolution.

00:13:42:1 - 00:14:28:1
Unknown
We had a second, I believe we're having a discussion on the motion. Not all in favor of the motion. Let it be known to say, and I am all opposed to the same sign motion carried and so ordered. Continue brother. this will complete the committee's report on education and public relations. I would like to move that. We discharge a committee at this time and thank you for your cooperation.

00:14:29:1 - 00:14:44:0
Unknown
You have heard the chairman of the committee request that the well, he offer a motion that the committee be discharged.

00:14:46:0 - 00:14:50:1
Unknown
Well, you can do that. We'll accept that as part of the motion.

00:14:53:0 - 00:15:20:1
Unknown
They were more we had a motion in the second to discharge the committee. We are having a discussion on that motion. Not all in favor of the motion. Let it be known by saying I am all opposed to the same sign. Motion carried and so ordered. Thank you. And your committee very much, brother Grey. This time we call on the chairman of the organizing committee.

00:15:20:1 - 00:15:58:1
Unknown
I believe they're ready to give us their final report on so. Mr. Chairman, delegates, yesterday when the committee presented to you resolution number 20. At that time, we had some still unfinished business. This morning, the committee met prior to the convening of the convention. We considered an item that was before us that was presented by an individual from down in south east Mississippi.

00:16:00:0 - 00:16:33:0
Unknown
And in view of the fact that the executive board of the Council will be considering this member's problem at their next meeting. The organizing committee took action or took the action to not make any recommendations to you concerning this particular item. And at this time I move that the organizing committee be discharged as we have nothing further to report.

00:16:35:0 - 00:17:04:1
Unknown
You have heard the motion of the chairman of the organizing committee that the organizing committee be this thing working. Yeah, it's all right now part of information and a request before he is discharged if he has prepared a resolution pertaining to this matter, even though he hasn't presented it here. And it is a matter for the executive board, whoever they may be, to consider.

00:17:04:1 - 00:17:10:0
Unknown
I would like to hear that resolution of the matter read to this body.

00:17:13:1 - 00:17:38:0
Unknown
Well, we have a motion on the floor now to discharge a committee of points been raised concerning the matter that the brother refers to. I don't want to get caught, and I must, Mr. Chairman, I'll make a substitute motion. Substitute motion in his order, and that we call on him to read this resolution to this body. All right.

00:17:38:0 - 00:18:15:0
Unknown
The brothers offer this service to do motion that they are going to have chairman of the organizing committee and read you a resolution concerning the matter that the committee considered. Brother Stanley, would you Brother Stanley said say will have to find it while we're waiting on the chairman Chairman brother all rise to table the substitute motion and go ahead with the previous motion that was made before the House.

00:18:15:0 - 00:18:43:1
Unknown
The motion to table is in order not debatable, but in order that we might understand where we are. We had a little problem that was brought here by someone outside of our group, which has already been considered by the executive Board. The executive board decided in their last meeting that they would take this matter up at the next executive board meeting.

00:18:44:1 - 00:19:11:1
Unknown
But these people saw fit to appear before the organizing committee and asked them to present it here. And the organizing committee has been informed of this fact, and they have now brought this up in this fashion. And are you ready? Vote to vote on the motion to table. All in favor of the motion. Let it be known. by saying I all opposed.

00:19:12:0 - 00:19:58:0
Unknown
Oh, all in favor of tabling the motion. Please raise your right hand. All right, All oppose. Raise your right hand. Emotion is carried now. Now, on the motion to discharge the committee that we're having a discussion all in favor of the motion. Let it be known. They and I all opposed emotions gathered and started. And thank you very much, Brother Stanley and your committee, for its wonderful work.

00:20:00:0 - 00:20:51:1
Unknown
I see we have Sister Murray with us. We didn't have her scheduled and quiet this early, but she's not but 5 minutes early anyhow. And it appears to me that we have just about all the delegate share. I certainly didn't want to put her in on until everybody had put it well, got out now. Sister Murray? Yeah, meeting with you and I will.

00:20:51:1 - 00:21:31:1
Unknown
And All right before I, before I introduce Sister Murray. Yeah. We got a, an announcement or a committee that's going to have to get ourselves organized. That's the election committee as Brother Marley in the House. Was Brother Marley able to get over this morning? It won't be till 10 a.m.. It's ten, 20, 20 now. Don't wait. Yeah, well, in the absence of Brother Marley, I want to appoint brother E. V. Edwards, chairman of the Election Committee.

00:21:33:1 - 00:22:00:1
Unknown
And in the absence of Brother Marley, what appears to me that we should replace him by voting. We want seven people on that committee, if possible. And Brother Patten back there, would you be able to substitute for Brother Marley in his absence on the election committee? Fred Yeah, all right. And Brother Edwards has requested a meeting of the election committee over here in the corner.

00:22:01:1 - 00:22:29:0
Unknown
You want it right away, but for just a few minutes I'll call the names off. Well, that's W.H. Wood, J.W. Flint, Bobby Long, E.V. Edwards, James Ward and Ray Huff. Brother Chappy, as has requested that Brother Flint take his place. He was on the original committee. Those people will gather in the corner will be and proceed to organize themselves for the election.

00:22:29:0 - 00:23:13:0
Unknown
This afternoon. I feel like that the young lady sitting up on a platform needs no introduction. To our convention here this morning the most of our delegates at least. She has been with us on numerous occasions. She has worked with several of our groups and we're happy to say that at long last, some of our people have started to move in in the political field, so to speak, as far as getting their card files and all that information accumulated.

00:23:13:0 - 00:23:54:0
Unknown
I can't stress this morning too much the importance of our lady folks in this political problem that we have. And certainly we are happy to see as many of our lady delegates at this convention as we do have, and also that we have the wives of a number of our delegates and also now, without any further ado, it gives me a great deal of pleasure to present to you at this time our good friend and sister Esther.

00:23:54:0 - 00:24:16:0
Unknown
Murray, President Ramsey, and delegates to this convention.

00:24:18:0 - 00:24:52:0
Unknown
Before I make my comments to you this morning, I should like to congratulate this convention. I should like to congratulate you on the number of women who are present here today. It's always an indication to me of the progressiveness or the reactionary tendencies of a state organization. And believe it or not, even labor can sometimes be a little reactionary.

00:24:52:0 - 00:25:25:0
Unknown
It's always an indication to me whether or not a convention and a state organization is progressive and forward moving and likely to win. And I see present a lot of women. And so before I make any further remarks, I'm going to ask all of the women, first of all, those who are delegates in their own right to stand when you do that, girls, those of you who are delegates in your own right here.

00:25:26:0 - 00:25:29:1
Unknown
Good, good. Now remain standing, please.

00:25:32:1 - 00:26:04:0
Unknown
Thank you. Now, with those wives who are present also stand those of you who are here as wives, our guests of the convention. Good. Thank you all very much. Now, if you will sit down, I'll tell you a little story. Yesterday, when I left Washington, D.C., to come here, I carried with me the Washington Post, the evening paper.

00:26:04:1 - 00:26:42:0
Unknown
And while I was in the plane, I began reading it and I found a story which interested me very much. This was the story of a housewife, a mother who was in her kitchen preparing an evening meal, and outside of the house near the garage, her 16 year old son was working in the car. He had jacked up the car, had taken off the two rear wheels and was under the car working on it, and suddenly there came into the kitchen.

00:26:42:0 - 00:27:12:0
Unknown
Some children, neighbor children screaming at the mother that the boy was being killed and she rushed out into the yard and sure enough, the jack had slipped and the boy was caught under the car and the mother crying as she did. It took hold of that car and single handedly lifted it and the children pulled the boy out.

00:27:12:0 - 00:27:30:0
Unknown
And when they interviewed her in the hospital for some broken bones, they asked her how much she weighed. The mother weighed 128 pounds and the car weighed over 3000.

00:27:32:0 - 00:28:17:0
Unknown
Now the mother is alive and the boy is alive. That it struck me as I read that story that I have never heard a more telling illustration of the kind of power that an aroused and emotionally determined woman has. What she did was impossible, but she did it. And sitting in this room, men of labor, I tell you that there is the power in these women sitting here beside you under your direction and under your guidance.

00:28:17:1 - 00:29:09:0
Unknown
And because you make us feel you need us, because you arouse in us the feeling that we are needed and that what we are doing is important. I tell you, there is the power to lift off the backs of labor in the state of Mississippi. The oppression that marks this state. And that's what I want to talk to you a few minutes about the state of Mississippi has a new in terms of strength, a new, vigorous, able, organized nation of organized labor.

00:29:10:0 - 00:29:46:1
Unknown
Your state organization has good leadership. Your county organizations have good leadership. And there are enough of us now in this state. We are strong enough now, if we gather our forces together and unite them in one powerful blow, we can have a permanent effect upon this state and we can have it politically. Politically, where the difference lies for us.

00:29:48:0 - 00:30:27:1
Unknown
This morning, before I left the hotel, I checked on what would happen in the state of Mississippi if the Kennedy-Morse-Roosevelt minimum wage law should pass. And it stands a pretty good chance of passing the Kennedy-Morse Bill Roosevelt bill would provide a dollar and a quarter minimum wage for all people in the state of Mississippi employed in industries that cross state lines.

00:30:28:0 - 00:31:16:1
Unknown
Do you know how much would change? What would happen to the pocketbooks of the workers of this state at that bill passes, it would affect only 80,000 workers in your state. 80,000 workers who are now being paid a dollar an hour under the present minimum wage law. Federal law, But get a dollar and a quarter an hour. It was a very small percentage of the number of workers, but it would mean now listen to me, it would mean $30 million a year.

00:31:16:1 - 00:31:54:0
Unknown
You know, a quarter doesn't sound like too much, just a quarter. But you add a quarter to the pocketbooks every hour of every man and woman employed in this state under now a dollar an hour. And you will add $30 million to working people's pocketbooks. That means that that money is not going into the bank. That money is going into rent and clothing and the milk bill and the food bill at the corner drugstore and shoes for the kids.

00:31:54:1 - 00:32:46:1
Unknown
It will be spent in this state and it will increase the economy of the state. It will make more jobs for everybody in the state. We'll all be better off because $30 million additional income has come into the state because the Kennedy-Morse-Roosevelt bill has been passed. It might be of some interest to you to know that the secretary of labor by name of Mitchell, supposedly the friend of working people, said yesterday in Washington that if the dollar and $0.25 an hour passed, he would recommend to the president that he veto it because he thinks the dollar and $0.15 is enough, well enough for Mr. Mitchell.

00:32:46:1 - 00:33:18:0
Unknown
Remember it. If you ever see his name on a national ticket, remember the man who was a fool would deny us that. A little additional $0.10 an hour that we want provided for us in the bill. But this is only one example. Only one example. There's another measure that the AFL-CIO is pushing hard for and which will undoubtedly be voted on in the Congress, which will meet in January.

00:33:18:1 - 00:33:26:0
Unknown
And we've got an election coming up in this state in November. And in November, we've got an opportunity to show our strength.

00:33:30:0 - 00:34:13:0
Unknown
Those of you in this audience and I see some of you in this audience who've already been doing your bit to see that the Kennedy-Morse-Roosevelt bill is passed. I recognize some of the girls here from Amalgamated who've been working long and hard on that fight, and I congratulate them. But it isn't enough to send petitions. That's why I want to talk to you a little bit more about one other example of what we can do to help pass legislation and then when another example of legislation, then talk a little more of what we can do.

00:34:16:1 - 00:34:46:1
Unknown
Every one of us this April faced an income tax law. Now, most of us in this room, all of us in this room are under a withholding tax and our federal income tax is taken out of our salaries. We never see that money before our checks ever reach us. The money we owe the federal government has been taken out of that check.

00:34:48:0 - 00:35:53:1
Unknown
Therefore, any change in income tax law will be reflected at once in our checks. Now, under the present law, you are allowed $600 deduction per person in your family tax free money. You are allowed $600 for a very interesting reason. Have you ever ask yourself why you're allowed $600 instead of $800 or $1,000? Have you considered the fact that when the law was written as late as 1939, every one of you here who is single was allowed $1,000 deduction and a married couple had $2500 deduction with $400 additional for every child.

00:35:54:0 - 00:36:37:0
Unknown
That was in 1939. What's happened that in 1956 you're allowed only $600. Do you know that you're allowed your $600 deduction because the federal government takes the position that $600 is enough to provide you with a roof, clothing and food for one year? This is the bare minimum, essential minimum essential that you must have tax free. And so you're allowed $600 tax free and $600 for your wife and $600 for each of your dependent children.

00:36:38:1 - 00:37:09:1
Unknown
And so if we are to assume that you're a family of four and you have an income of $5,000 a year, that family of four is allowed on the basis of $600 per person, $2400 of tax free money out of your 5000. You're also allowed 10% of your 5000 for general deduction, and that leaves you with a taxable income of $420 a year.

00:37:10:0 - 00:37:49:1
Unknown
That is, your tax is $420 a year. Now, the AFL-CIO has a program, a tax program. The AFL CIO says $600 is ridiculous as a basic cost of living allowance in 1960. And so it's asking for only $800, not even a thousand we used to have $800 per person and at $800 per person. And by the way, we almost got it in 1954, we came within five votes in the Congress of the United States of getting that deduction.

00:37:51:0 - 00:38:24:0
Unknown
All right. So what would happen to your paycheck if the AFL CIO program goes through? I'd take a get our family of four our income of $5,000, a family of four, an income of $5,000 a year allowed $800. You've got $3200 tax free money. You add to that the $500 which comes with that 10%, you're allowed for general deduction and your total tax free money is $3800.

00:38:25:0 - 00:39:03:1
Unknown
And you subtract that from your 5000 and it leaves you, at my figures, about 1300 dollars of taxable money. Am I right? Anybody following my figures? 1200 dollars of taxable money. All right. And that to end at the rate of 20% because the poorest man in America pays 20% of his taxable income to the federal government, the poorest of us begin the 20% and 20% of that gives us a taxable income of $260.

00:39:03:1 - 00:39:53:0
Unknown
Am I right? $240. All right. What's the difference in your paycheck? If the AFL-CIO program goes through the difference in your paycheck on a basis of 2080 hours a year, which is the bargaining contract upon which most contracts provide for a year hourly work on the basis of 2080 hours a year, your paycheck will change if they have AFL-CIO provisions passes to allow you an $0.08 an hour increase, $0.08 an hour less will be taken out of your paycheck.

00:39:54:1 - 00:40:40:1
Unknown
Now, many unions gone on strike for $0.08 an hour, but $0.08 an hour is waiting for you without a single act of negotiating with your employer. What you have to do is to go sit with your congressman to get him to support $800 as a deduction instead of $600 as a deduction. We could go on all this morning discussing the immediate financial results to us of certain specific legislative items I've mentioned only to the passage of the minimum wage and what would happen to the state of Mississippi and the passage of the AFL-CIO.

00:40:40:1 - 00:41:11:0
Unknown
Weight of tax recommendations. I might incidentally tell you that the Chamber of Commerce and Merchants, the Manufacturers Association, also have a tax program. They've got it all written out. It's on the desk of every congressman, and it asks not for $800 as our deduction, not for $600 as our deduction, but $500 is our deduction, which would raise your tax approximately $0.04 an hour over what you are now paying.

00:41:11:1 - 00:41:36:1
Unknown
So you've got to really add $0.12 an hour spread here between what the AFL-CIO is trying to get for us and what the merchants and Manufacturers Association is trying to get passed. How do these women, of which I spoke, fit into this picture to begin with as trade unionists, we're in the same boat. We have wages and hours that are involved in this, too.

00:41:37:0 - 00:42:22:0
Unknown
But we have a much deeper concern. We women can do a kind of job for you politically that you're just not going to do without us. We can do the preparation, the preparation of the COPE program in Jackson, Mississippi, and in Pascagoula, Mississippi. We're already making an effort in that direction and I hope will demonstrate this year what can be done in both of these communities by women working as volunteers.
